# 10 — Deployments and quote assets

<!-- generated:status-banner -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

> **RC6 is LIVE ON ROBINHOOD CHAIN.** RC6 is deployed on Robinhood Chain (4663) as of 2026-08-19, and its factory there is PUBLIC: that chain accepts ordinary creator launches. RC6 is NOT deployed on Ethereum, Base or BNB Smart Chain, and no date is set for any of them.
> Public creator launch is **open** on Robinhood Chain (4663) and **closed** on the other 3 configured chains.
> See [08 — Status and limitations](08-status.md).

<!-- /generated:status-banner -->

## There are no RC6 addresses to publish

This page used to carry a table of platform contract addresses. It does not any more, and the
reason is not caution — it is that the addresses do not exist yet.

RC6 is prepared and not deployed. Every RC6 contract address is still to be determined and will
change. A published address for a contract that has not been deployed is worse than a blank: it gets
copied into a script, the script outlives the correction, and the person who runs it a month later
has no way to tell that the number was aspirational.

The addresses that appeared here in earlier revisions are **RC5** addresses. RC5 is the previous
generation. Those contracts are real and source-verified on their chains; they are not what an RC6
bundle launches through, and they will not become RC6 by being relabelled.

**When RC6 deploys**, the address reference is regenerated from the production deployment manifests
by the procedure in [08 — Status and limitations](08-status.md#post-deployment-sync--the-procedure-not-a-promise),
and this page will point at that generated record rather than restating it.

## Reading launch state at runtime instead of from a document

Whatever this page says, a program should ask the chain.

```js
import { PLATFORM_DEPLOYMENTS, acceptsPublicLaunches, platformDeployment } from "@relics/project-schema";
```

Two cautions about those exports, both of which matter more than the API shape:

1. **They describe the RC5 deployment record**, because that is the generation that is deployed.
   Read them as "what is on chain today", never as "what an RC6 launch will use".
2. **`acceptsPublicLaunches` is a convenience over a fact you can read yourself.** The authority is
   the factory's own launch-access state. A document — including this one — can be stale; a contract
   read cannot.

`npm run kit:status` prints the same record locally.

## Quote assets: a bundle requests, it never approves

A `.relics` bundle may name the quote asset it wants. The importer resolves that request against the
launchpad's registry on the target chain, and the registry decides.

```json
{
  "market": {
    "chainId": 4663,
    "quoteAsset": {
      "mode": "ADDRESS",
      "address": "0x…",
      "expectedKind": "STOCK_TOKEN"
    }
  }
}
```

**Ethereum and Base admit exactly one quote: the canonical WETH.** A non-WETH quote is refused there
by chain id, not by convention — there is no registry to consult and no request that succeeds.

**BNB Smart Chain admits its wrapped native, WBNB.** Not WETH; not "ETH". See
[06 — Fees and revenue](06-fees-and-revenue.md#which-asset-the-platform-is-paid-in).

**Robinhood Chain is the multi-quote chain.** Any asset the quote registry currently admits *and*
leaves enabled may be named: the wrapped native, the stablecoin, the Robinhood stock and ETF tokens,
and the ecosystem token. The complete official stock/ETF reference is exported from the schema
package rather than reproduced here, because a partial list copied into an app is a list that goes
stale silently:

```js
import { ROBINHOOD_STOCK_TOKEN_COUNT, robinhoodStockTokenBySymbol } from "@relics/project-schema";
```

If you need a selector, import the list and filter it. Do not paste a subset.

### What the quote registry can and cannot do

The registry decides exactly one thing: whether an asset may be **selected as the quote leg of a new
launch**. The selected asset is then written into that project's canonical `PoolKey` and is immutable
for the life of the project.

So disabling an asset blocks **new** launches against it and nothing else. It does not rewrite an
existing `PoolKey` — a `PoolKey` is not writable by anyone — and it does not migrate, drain,
re-route or re-price any existing pool, alter any existing art history, or touch a creator's
entitlements or claims. The property is structural: no function on the registry takes a project id
or a pool id, so there is no expressible call that reaches a launched project.

There is also **no arbitrary-address path**. The admitted-kind vocabulary has no "custom address"
member and the registry has no "admit whatever the caller passes" entrypoint. An unadmitted address
produces exactly one outcome: the launch reverts.

Two roles govern it, deliberately asymmetric. The upgrade authority (the protocol 2-of-3 Safe) admits
assets, updates them, re-enables them and approves conversion routes. A separate guardian holds an
emergency brake **only**: it may disable an asset or a route, and can never enable, admit, widen a
bound, or lower a risk tier. The fast path is strictly de-risking; every re-widening is an act of the
Safe.

`riskTier` is a tier, not a safety label. The protocol never marks an asset "safe" — there is no such
field.

## Quote admission and the WETH route are separate questions

A quote asset can be enabled for new launches before the platform's route from that quote to WETH has
been proven. That is fine and normal: the treasury half of the platform share is claimable in the
quote regardless, and the buy-and-entomb half is allowed to wait, visibly, in its own state.

Do not read "enabled" as "a WETH route exists".

And that is a **different route** from the one a creator's `QUOTE_ONLY` election needs, which is the
project token into the quote — the conversion that mode promises the creator. Two requirements, two
routes, two payers.

## Guidance for interfaces

- Display the quote asset you actually read. Never relabel a stock-token entitlement as WETH.
- Never treat `PREPARED` as public launch availability.
- Never print a wrapped-native symbol you did not read from the chain profile.
- Never publish an RC6 address until you have read it from the deployment manifest for a deploy that
  has happened.
